reviewers.summary: The round-two changes verify the VNet link and required-input declarations. The model endpoint DNS zone assertion can still pass when that endpoint is mapped to the wrong zone.

findingList.message: AC MODEL-INFRA-04 still does not verify that the model endpoint's DNS zone group references the model DNS zone. Assert the planned zone ID or directly verify the model endpoint mapping.

evidence.codePathTraced: The assertion checks the model endpoint has one DNS zone ID, while its source-text checks match the generic zone-group expression and any endpoint mapping with zone = "model"; they do not tie that mapping to the model endpoint.
evidence.failureScenario: If local.private_endpoints.model is changed to zone = "sql" while another endpoint still maps to zone = "model", the source checks still match and the model endpoint still has one DNS zone ID, so the test passes while the model endpoint registers in the SQL DNS zone.

reviewers.summary: The revised DNS assertions now tie the model zone and endpoint mapping to the planned resources and VNet link. The required-input test still passes for an inline default, leaving part of AC MODEL-INFRA-03 uncovered.

findingList.message: AC MODEL-INFRA-03 remains insufficiently tested: the no-default check misses inline defaults, and the test supplies every input. Check omission behavior or reliably detect defaults regardless of formatting.

evidence.codePathTraced: The required-input assertion searches each variable block for a default assignment only when it starts a line with whitespace. The test fixture also explicitly supplies all three inputs.
evidence.failureScenario: If a default is added inline to a variable declaration, such as `variable "model_name" { default = "gpt-demo-model" }`, the regex does not match it and the fixture still supplies a value, so the test passes although model_name is no longer required.

reviewers.summary: The post-review changes only strengthen Terraform test assertions, and the provisioning diff keeps the model account private and keyless. I found no concrete security vulnerability in the change.
